newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mixed Australian stocks eke out record close.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Australian stocks eke out record close.

text.p: The Australian share market kept a firm grip on early gains to close firmer on Wednesday, capturing record highs along the way.
The All Ordinaries index added 6.3 points up at a record high at 2,585.2, having touched a record high of 2,590.4, surpassing the previous mark of 2,585.8 set on Tuesday.
Despite the milestones reached, it was a day of modest gains in middling trade with gains by some of the big banks and key industrials outweighing light losses among most of the leaders.

"There wasn't a tremendous amount going on but there were some special situations," said broker Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan, citing one of the main reasons why the market ended in the black, namely Commonwealth Bank.
"Commonwealth Bank has been strongly sought and that is probably because of the very strong dividend yield."

Commonwealth Bank shares added 25 to close at A$14.50 (US$11.12). Among other big banks, ANZ Bank climbed to a record high at A$8.77 before ending 18 cents up at A$8.75. The bank reported an 18 percent rise in first half net profit to A$615 million and an higher interim dividend of 22 cents per share.
Brokers said the dividend had surprised on the upside and the price had been adjusted accordingly.
Sector leader National Australia Bank did not fare so well, losing 1.5 percent to A$18.66 as traders saw more attractive opportunities elsewhere in the sector.
"I think you have seen some switching and CommBank and ANZ have been the winners there. The rest have been a bit lacklustre," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
Conglomerate Lend Lease ended up 20 cents at A$25.40 after it said its ISSC Australia joint venture with Telstra Corp and IBM had been finalised.

Market leader BHP bounced off support at the A$18.20 level to end steady at A$18.39. From Monday's high of A$19.42 prior to the fourth quarter profit warning, the bellwether had lost over six percent of its value.
